title: Was the Famous Bigfoot Film Staged? New Doc Says Maybe
excerpt: Was the Famous Bigfoot Film Staged? New Doc Says Maybe
content:
I'm sure you've heard the saying "You're pulling my leg." People use that expression when they're convinced someone is telling them a whopper, a lie. As it turns out, there's a new documentary that suggests that someone may have been pulling a foot. A big one.

I remember hearing tales of Bigfoot during my childhood. Though I never knew anyone personally who claimed to have seen him, I always heard adults talk about people who knew people that may have known people who had. As ridiculous as the thought of some gigantic ape-like creature roaming through the woods seemed, I do remember being afraid I might accidentally stumble into him during one of my family's camping trips.  I always hesitated to wander off in the woods alone.

Of course, Bigfoot was part of the pop culture I consumed in the late '70s and early '80s. Two of my favorite shows, The Six Million Dollar Man and The Bionic Woman, had crossover episodes in which they teamed up to take on Bigfoot.

I realize that clip is ridiculous, but I was about 7 years old when that first aired. I was convinced Bigfoot was real. A lot of people were and still are.

It now seems, THAT may be ridiculous. Capturing Bigfoot, a 2026 documentary by Marq Evans, dives deep into the mythology of the famed creature. The modern Bigfoot craze dates back to 1967. That's when Roger Patterson and Bob Gimlin claimed to have filmed a large, unidentified figure walking through a forest in northern California. As it turns out, that video, which is responsible for much of the folklore surrounding Bigfoot—the rash of supposed sightings, the Bigfoot festivals around the country, Steve Austin and Jamie Sommers battling him on my television screen in the ’70s, and so on—may be fake.

According to the documentary, descendants of the filmmakers have discovered a 40-second reel of film that appears to contain rehearsal footage.  Could it be that 1967 "sighting" was actually staged?

Look. It didn't take me long to outgrow the fears I had as a 7-year-old. I didn't believe in Bigfoot much longer than I did Santa Claus, the Easter Bunny, or the Tooth Fairy. But, there are still a ton of folks in this country who are convinced he's out there, somewhere.

What do you think? Is Bigfoot fact or fiction? If your inquiring mind wants to know, you can catch Capturing Bigfoot, which is available now on Prime Video.
